question: Owner's ratchet metric #315/#316: how many detcore INFO-log records does each backend stay bitwise-identical to the ptrace golden, per rung?
answer: Every backend depth is CONSTANT across four orders of magnitude of Z (145 -> 400940): dbi 3, sabre 1, liteinst 8. The ratchet is measuring a process-prologue divergence, not workload parity, so heavier rungs cannot move it. e9patch instruments nothing (mapped_sites=0) and would have falsely scored a perfect Z/Z.
definition: record = line containing DETLOG or COMMIT turn; Z = golden record count; Y = longest common record prefix; only the real wall-clock prefix is stripped; full INFO log, not stdout. Unchanged from prefix-parity-depth-remeasured_20260806.md.
binary_provenance: baked-in version string carries a -dirty marker; this binary reports clean
precondition: golden captured twice per rung and required bit-identical; all 8 rungs passed
relaxations: none for the ratchet number; the dbi fold table is explicitly labelled DIAGNOSTIC
not_established: backend arms are n=1 per rung (the golden is n=2); depth constancy across 8 rungs is the reason replication was not prioritized
the layered fold decomposition was done on /bin/true only
depth counts records, not COMMIT-turn lines specifically; a commits-only definition would need re-baselining per #316
kvm confirmed TOOL-ERROR once, then excluded from the per-rung loop rather than re-timed 8 times
e9patch not investigated beyond mapped_sites=0; whether it can patch these guests at all is untested
